question: To unlock Chu Bai Qiang (褚白抢), what is the order in which the player collects the Captain Spirits (精魄)? 1. Captain Kalpa-Wave (劫波) 2. Captain Lotus-Vision (莲眼) 3. Captain Void-Illusion (妄相) 4. Captain Wise-Voice (妙音)

rollouts.answer: 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 1 (Lotus-Vision, Wise-Voice, Void-Illusion, Kalpa-Wave), i.e. it put Lotus-Vision (莲眼) FIRST at ~24,320-24,355s
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search(event_steps/topic_facts/episodes) x4 -> run_sql(episodes name-LIKE) -> semantic_search(episodes) x4 -> run_sql(episodes 莲/妄 LIKE) -> run_sql(event_chains) -> run_sql(event_steps 20000-36000) -> run_sql(event_steps 22400-25000) -> run_sql(event_steps 25380-34920 boss/spirit/defeat) -> read_skill(visual-verification) -> clip_qa(23900-25800, rejected >20min) -> clip_qa(23900-24900) -> clip_qa(24900-25800) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa(23900-24900) answered that the boss defeated at ~24320-24355s is Captain Lotus-Vision (莲眼) -- this is a boss fight with no corroborating text-DB name anywhere near 24320s and is not one of the 4 clue windows; likely a misidentified/hallucinated captain sighting.

clip_qa(24900-25800) answered '先击败妙音，后击败妄相' i.e. read the on-screen boss name card for the second clue window (~25532-25736s, which is inside clue_interval [25524,25746]) as 妄相 (Void-Illusion). Directly re-reading the source frames myself at t=25730s shows the on-screen defeat card actually reads '头目·魔将·莲眼' (Captain/Chief Demon-General Lotus-Vision) -- the visual sub-agent misread the boss name.

rollouts.failure_point: Visual sub-agent (clip_qa) misread the Chinese boss-name card in the second clue window (莲眼 misread as 妄相), and separately reported an uncorroborated earlier 'Lotus-Vision' sighting at ~24,320s that does not correspond to any clue window; both errors combined to invert the true order and put Lotus-Vision first.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Pulled raw frames at t=25710-25735s directly (memcli frame) and read them myself: the defeat banner at 25730s literally shows Chinese text '已击败' / '头日·魔将·莲眼', confirming the second clue window is Captain Lotus-Vision (莲眼), not Void-Illusion (妄相) as clip_qa reported.

rollouts.answer: 3 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 (Void-Illusion, Wise-Voice, Lotus-Vision, Kalpa-Wave); claims Void-Illusion interaction 'just before' the Wise-Voice encounter at ~25,020s
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search(episodes/event_steps) x4 -> run_sql(event_steps join event_chains) -> semantic_search(episodes/topic_facts/visual_clips) x4 -> run_sql(episodes 莲眼/妄相/妙音/劫波 LIKE) -> semantic_search(episodes) x3 -> run_sql(event_steps join event_chains 38000-43000) -> run_sql(event_chains summary LIKE) -> run_sql(event_steps 25200-30000) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: run_sql on event_steps 25200-30000 was the last evidence pull before submit; no row in this or any prior query actually names 莲眼 or 妄相 (confirmed: those two strings appear nowhere in the entire memory DB across all tables), so the model attached '妄相' to a generic intro/cutscene moment near 25,020s purely by guesswork, ahead of the correctly-identified 妙音 defeat at ~25,260-25,290s.

rollouts.failure_point: 妄相 and 莲眼 never appear as text anywhere in the DB (episodes/entities/event_steps/semantic_triples/topic_facts/visual_clips all return zero hits), so the model had to guess their identity/position with no textual grounding and no clip_qa call; it guessed wrong, putting the unnamed 'Void-Illusion' before the well-evidenced Wise-Voice defeat.
rollouts.evidence_checked: SQL LIKE search for '妄相' and '莲眼' across every text-bearing column in every table returns 0 rows; the DB genuinely never transcribes these two captain names.

rollouts.answer: Stated 'The order is 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4' but the itemized list underneath is Wise-Voice, Lotus-Vision, Void-Illusion, Kalpa-Wave (i.e. captain-labels 4,2,3,1) -- same underlying order as the reference, just phrased with a mismatched leading numbering line
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search(episodes/topic_facts) x3 -> semantic_search(episodes) x4 (per-captain) -> run_sql(episodes 30sec LIKE names) -> run_sql(event_steps LIKE names) -> semantic_search(episodes) x2 -> semantic_search(object_states) x2 -> run_sql(episodes 21600-...) -> run_sql(event_steps 25200-35080) -> run_sql(event_steps 26700-34920) -> semantic_search(visual_clips) -> run_sql(object_states 25200-3...) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: submit_answer places Void-Illusion at '~31,680s'; I checked the DB text at 31,650-31,710s and it is a generic golden-armored boss fight with a plain '已击败' defeat, with no name text anywhere resembling 妄相 -- so the timestamp for Void-Illusion is fabricated/unconfirmed, but the relative ORDER (妙音 < 莲眼 < 妄相 < 劫波) happens to be correct since it is just the natural chronological order of a plausible defeat event picked from each bracket.

rollouts.failure_point: No true failure in the underlying sequence -- the substantive order matches the reference -- but the answer's leading summary line ('order is 1->2->3->4') uses the captain's own list-position numbering rather than the question's canonical Kalpa/Lotus/Void/Wise-voice numbering used in the reference ('4,2,3,1'), which is confusing/format-mismatched even though the itemized names below are correct; likely cost it a point from a strict judge.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Checked DB text around the claimed Void-Illusion timestamp (31,650-31,710s): a generic boss fight with no name evidence for 妄相, confirming this timestamp is an unverified placeholder rather than grounded evidence.

rollouts.answer: 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4 (Lotus-Vision, Kalpa-Wave, Void-Illusion, Wise-Voice); puts Kalpa-Wave second and Wise-Voice last

decisive_steps.what_happened: submit_answer puts Kalpa-Wave (劫波) second, despite the text clue at 34920-35100s ('魔将劫波' name-card fades in, boss fight, victory') being unambiguously the LAST clue window in time and the only clip_qa-free evidence available; the model instead over-weighted an earlier, unrelated mention of 劫波 in the topic_facts/semantic_triples search (e.g. the 32400-36000s 1h-episode summary that lists 劫波 among several bosses fought in that hour, without ordering) and misread that as an early occurrence.

rollouts.failure_point: Same fundamental gap as rollout-01: 莲眼/妄相 are never named in text, so their placement is a guess; additionally this rollout mis-time-ordered the well-evidenced 劫波 encounter (placing it 2nd instead of last) by conflating a coarse-granularity summary mention with the actual fight timestamp, showing a wrong-time-window error on top of the name-guessing problem.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Confirmed via the episodes table that the only concrete 劫波 boss-name-card + defeat text sits at 34920-35100s, i.e. after all three other captains' windows, contradicting rollout-03's placement of Kalpa-Wave second.

rollouts.answer: 4 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 (Wise-Voice, Lotus-Vision, Void-Illusion, Kalpa-Wave) -- matches the reference exactly

LIKE) -> run_sql(event_steps 劫波/... LIKE) -> run_sql(topic_facts 劫波/莲眼/... LIKE) -> semantic_search(episodes) x3 -> semantic_search(topic_facts) -> run_sql(event_steps captain/... LIKE) -> semantic_search(visual_clips/event_steps) x2 -> semantic_search(topic_facts) -> run_sql(episodes 30sec ...) x2 -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: submit_answer places Void-Illusion at '~29,190s', a defeat event ('已击败' on-screen at 29190-29220s) that I confirmed in the DB text has no name evidence tying it to 妄相 either -- so, like rollout-02, this rollout's exact timestamp for the un-named captain is unconfirmed/guessed, but the relative sequencing of the four names (which is what the reference answer actually grades) happens to be correct.

rollouts.evidence_checked: Checked DB text at the claimed Void-Illusion timestamp (29,160-29,220s): a generic 'towering creature formed from withered branches/antlers' boss with a plain defeat notice, no name text -- same lack of grounding as the other rollouts, but the relative order it landed on is correct.

db_evidence.notes: Window 1 (25069-25333, Wise-Voice/妙音) and window 4 (34935-35074, Kalpa-Wave/劫波) ARE explicitly named in the episodes text (boss-name overlay text '妖王·魔将·妙音' with '已击败', and '魔将劫波' name card + fight + victory sequence respectively) -- these are reliably retrievable by SQL/semantic search. Windows 2 and 3 (Lotus-Vision/莲眼 and Void-Illusion/妄相) are NEVER named anywhere in any DB table (verified with SQL LIKE '%莲眼%' / '%妄相%' against episodes, entities, event_chains, event_steps, object_states, semantic_triples, topic_chains, topic_facts, visual_clips -- all return 0 rows). I pulled and read raw source frames myself: at t=25730s the on-screen defeat banner reads '头日·魔将·莲眼' confirming window 2 = Lotus-Vision (莲眼), and at t=34564s a purple item-pickup prompt ('神魂·三将' / spirit-soul third general) appears right after a distinct boss (a withered-branch/antler creature) is struck down, consistent with window 3 = Void-Illusion (妄相) being collected there. The reference answer '4,2,3,1' is fully consistent with this frame-level ground truth (chronological window order = collection order).

root_causes: Two of the four captain names (莲眼 Lotus-Vision, 妄相 Void-Illusion) are never transcribed into any DB table by the captioning/extraction pipeline, so pure text/SQL/semantic-search retrieval (used by rollouts 1-4) cannot ground their identity or position at all -- those rollouts effectively guessed the middle two positions.

Because the true collection order equals simple chronological order of the four clue windows, a rollout that just default-orders the two un-named captains as (莲眼 then 妄相) in the middle -- matching the order they happen to be listed in the question stem -- gets lucky and lands on the correct sequence (rollouts 2 and 4); a rollout that reorders them differently (rollouts 1 and 3) gets it wrong.

The one rollout that did use the correct tool for this gap (clip_qa / visual verification, rollout 0) still failed because the visual sub-agent misread the on-screen Chinese boss-name card in the second clue window (read '莲眼' as '妄相'), and additionally reported an uncorroborated 'Lotus-Vision' sighting outside any clue window (~24,320s) that pulled it out of order -- a visual-OCR/reading error, not a retrieval-strategy error.

Rollout 2's answer text has a format/self-consistency slip: it labels the sequence 'order is 1->2->3->4' (using the captain-list's own indices in listed order) instead of the question's canonical 4-2-3-1 labeling scheme, even though the itemized names underneath are in the correct order -- likely a minor judge penalty despite correct substance.

Rollout 3 additionally mis-times the well-evidenced Kalpa-Wave (劫波) encounter, placing it 2nd instead of last, by apparently conflating a coarse 1-hour-window summary mention of 劫波 with the actual fight timestamp.
what_worked: SQL LIKE search and semantic_search over episodes/event_steps/topic_facts reliably located and named the two well-transcribed captains (Wise-Voice 妙音 and Kalpa-Wave 劫波), which all 5 rollouts correctly identified and placed at the correct chronological extremes (Wise-Voice early, Kalpa-Wave last).

Rollouts 2 and 4 defaulted to inserting the two un-named captains (Lotus-Vision, Void-Illusion) in the same order they appear in the question's own numbered list, which happened to coincide with the true video order, earning them the top two scores despite no real textual/visual grounding for those two names specifically.
transferable_lessons: Before trusting a text-only order for a multi-entity ordering question, explicitly SQL-search for every entity's literal name string across all tables; if a name returns zero rows anywhere, that entity's position is fundamentally unknowable from text and MUST be resolved with clip_qa on the specific clue window, not guessed.

When using clip_qa to read an on-screen Chinese boss-name banner, cross-check the read name against the full candidate list (all 4 captain names here) rather than accepting the sub-agent's single free-form transcription at face value -- 莲眼 and 妄相 are visually/structurally similar two-character boss-title suffixes and were confused by the visual sub-agent in this trace.

For 'order in which X happens' temporal-reasoning questions, if the clue windows are already given in monotonically increasing time order, the answer often IS simply the chronological order of whichever entity is confirmed in each window -- so getting each window's IDENTITY right matters far more than reasoning about ordering.

A correct substantive answer wrapped in a self-contradictory summary line (e.g., stating 'order is 1->2->3->4' while listing names in the true 4->2->3->1 order) risks judge penalty even when the itemized content is right -- keep the leading numeric summary consistent with the question's own labeling scheme.
open_questions: Why does rollout 0's clip_qa sub-agent misread '莲眼' as '妄相' on a fairly legible on-screen banner at t=25730s -- is this a systematic OCR weakness for this pair of similar 2-character titles, or a one-off sampling artifact (wrong frame sampled)?

Whether the pipeline that generates episodes/event_steps/topic_facts captions is generally weak at reading small Chinese boss-name-card overlays (as opposed to the large centered '已击败'/victory banners it does capture), which would explain the systematic absence of 莲眼/妄相 anywhere in the DB while 妙音/劫波 (which get large on-screen name reveals) are present.
